meta.title: A Message from the Nurse's Room
meta.textType: story: a stomachache, a voice message, and an email to the parents

paragraphs: On Monday, February eighth, at ten o'clock, Pat told his teacher that his stomach hurt. His teacher took him to May's classroom, because May is his sister. Teacher Kim let May go with him. May carried Pat's school bag, and they walked to the nurse's room. The room was small and white. It had a desk and a glass cabinet with a red cross on it. A poster on the wall said "WASH YOUR HANDS." Nurse Jill gave Pat a paper cup of water. Pat sat on a chair, and May stood next to him. Nurse Jill sat at her desk and wrote his name on a paper. "Where is the pain, and when did it start?" she asked. "Here," said Pat, and he put his hand on his stomach. "It is sore, and it started two hours ago."

Nurse Jill opened the first-aid kit and took out a small thermometer. She held it near Pat's ear for a few seconds. "What did you eat last night?" she asked. Pat looked at his shoes. "Three green mangoes, with chili," he said. May looked at the ceiling and did not say a word. "Your temperature is normal," Nurse Jill told Pat. "You have a stomachache because green mangoes and chili are hard for a stomach," she said. "My advice is simple: drink water, and sit quietly." "You do not need medicine today." "If it hurts again, you need an appointment with a doctor."

Next, Nurse Jill wrote an email to Pat's parents at her computer. A blue folder marked "HEALTH FOLDER" lay beside the keyboard. The email started with "Dear Pat's mom and dad," and it had three short lines. The first line said, "Pat is in the nurse's room." The second line said, "He has a stomachache, but no fever." The third line said, "He is drinking water and resting." The email ended with "Best wishes, Nurse Jill." Then she wrote the time in the folder.

"An email is good for a record," said Nurse Jill, "but a phone call is fast." She called Pat's parents, but nobody answered. So she left a voice message. "Hello, this is Nurse Jill at the school." "Pat is in the nurse's room. He has a stomachache, but no fever. Please call me." Their mom called back at once. "Thank you, Nurse Jill," she said. "I was worried, but I am glad that he is alright." "I will come at half past eleven," she said.

Pat drank his water and sat quietly. "Are you alright now?" asked Nurse Jill. "Yes," said Pat. "My stomach is not sore now." "Good," said Nurse Jill. "Next time, eat one sweet mango, not three green ones." At half past eleven, their mom came to the door. Pat looked at his shoes again. "Three green mangoes," he said quietly, "with chili."

His teacher took him to May's classroom, because May is his sister.

"It is sore, and it started two hours ago."

She held it near Pat's ear for a few seconds.

Pat looked at his shoes.
"Three green mangoes, with chili," he said.
May looked at the ceiling and did not say a word.

"My advice is simple: drink water, and sit quietly."
"You do not need medicine today."
"If it hurts again, you need an appointment with a doctor."

A blue folder marked "HEALTH FOLDER" lay beside the keyboard.

The second line said, "He has a stomachache, but no fever."
